title: End wind gave no clear first-block bird richness link in four Canada and US samples in 1985-2024
abstract: We tested whether end wind predicted recorded bird taxa in the first ten survey stops after control for start weather. Four models used 64,681 accepted Canada and US surveys in 1985-2004 and 2005-2024. All four first-block intervals included zero after correction. First-block slopes ranged from -0.091 to -0.005 taxa per higher wind code. Last-block slopes ranged from -0.913 to -0.604. Last-minus-first slopes were negative in all samples. This pattern is consistent with a more negative association later in a route. It does not prove a detection mechanism. Wind persists, end wind can mark early conditions, and blocks differ in place and time. Selection, exposure error and shared routes limit inference. We reused a verified published panel and did not rebuild raw data. The package includes the panel, code, provenance, all fits and a figure. We did not test climate trends, wind damage or pollution.

display.caption: First-block end-wind coefficients with four-test intervals, and five block profiles with individual 95 percent intervals. End wind is measured later and can also mark early conditions. These are survey associations.
